details.label: Discussion
details.text: The latest Day Cloud Phase satellite imagery indicates deepening boundary-layer cumulus along a surface front/wind shift in parts of central ND -- immediately east-northeast of Bismarck. In the near term, isolated convective initiation will be possible along the wind shift, as earlier capping at the base of the EML (sampled by the BIS 18Z sounding) continues to erode amid an increasingly warm/unstable PBL. Steep midlevel lapse rates atop the warm/moist PBL and an elongating/mostly straight holograph (around 40-50 kt of effective shear) will conditionally support discrete supercells capable of producing large to very large hail and locally severe wind gusts. However, weak large-scale forcing for ascent limits confidence in both the coverage and evolution of this initial storm development. Over the next few hours, increasing ascent accompanying a midlevel wave to the north should support an increase in storm coverage along the surface front. The aforementioned environment will promote an increasing risk of scattered supercells capable of producing large hail and severe wind gusts. With time and eastward extent, upscale growth into organized clusters could pose an increasing risk of severe wind. A watch will likely be needed in the next hour or so
